parsed.explanation: The combined regime stacks a federal document/entry exposure (M/F-only markers, visa refusal where records cast doubt on sex, possible lifetime fraud finding, stranded travellers, foreign advisories) over federal and state birth-sex facility rules with a documented 2025 restroom arrest and men's-ward holding. If detention follows, the corrections bureau's conversion-therapy mandate and documented immigration-custody abuse raise severity sharply. The division adds no non-discrimination law, a statutory religious-refusal licence, a hostile 8-1 high court and an under-18 care ban reaching a travelling minor. Offsetting: national hate-crime recourse with a 49-year conviction, pending litigation and injunctions, near-baseline violence, and majority local support for anti-discrimination. No organised visitor-sweep campaign is documented.

entry_documents.exposure: Feb 2025 order and cable: markers only M/F, no X; cases refused where documents cast reasonable doubt on sex; suspected misrepresentation can support a lifetime fraud-ineligibility finding; trans travellers report passports blocked or confiscated and being stranded; at least eight foreign governments issued travel advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports remain valid until expiry; the restriction remains challenged in national courts; a legal-aid organisation maintains an active guidance FAQ.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy can escalate: refusal or stranding → immigration detention → birth-sex custody and the custody harms recorded below.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: From 2026 the national corrections bureau mandates conversion-therapy practice for trans inmates (hair cutting, hormone removal, substituted psychiatric drugs); immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse; a trans woman was held 24 hours in a men's ward after a 2025 restroom arrest; name changes barred in custody.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute applies; constitutional challenges to the orders are pending; no visitor-specific custody remedy is documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any border or facility encounter ending in detention drops the traveller into this custody regime, where the division's hostile judiciary offers little local recourse.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities; the division's 2024 law requires school bathrooms by birth sex and statute defines sex by birth; four units criminalise use (trespass, requiring refusal to leave); maps show 9+1 units with all-government-building bans; one documented capitol arrest.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 29 units have no mapped ban; two restrictive division bills died in 2024; most bans reach only government-owned settings, leaving private venues open.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal funding rules and division law reinforce each other; a visitor entering a public school, capitol or federal building carries the exclusion regardless of document conformity.

care_services.exposure: Division bans under-18 gender-affirming care (2023) and closed the main clinic; the justice department subpoenaed under-19 patient records in 2025; a 2017 religious-liberties statute gives providers a statutory basis to refuse service; federal funding freezes target trans youth care.
care_services.protection: Adult emergency care is not documented as denied; legal-aid resources exist and several federal orders are enjoined or contested.
care_services.interaction: An adult travelling with a trans minor can face care denial and record-surrender risk; the refusal licence reaches visitors in services with no division-level protection.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal strategy prioritises identifying and neutralising groups 'radically pro-transgender'; officials use 'chemical and surgical mutilation' and 'radical gender ideology'; the division high court called a trans boy 'minor female' 8-1; a 2025 poll found 66% support ASAB markers on documents.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The reward memo never uses ideology as a criterion and the strategy disclaims targeting mere dissenters; several orders are enjoined; 67% of division residents back an anti-discrimination law.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing raises both probability and severity of every traveller encounter, from document adjudication to service refusal to custody placement.

minors_guardians.exposure: Division high court denied a trans teen's name change 8-1 (Apr 2025); under-18 care banned; school bathroom, sports and dress rules by birth sex; federal order directs criminal investigation of teachers facilitating social transition; under-19 medical records subpoenaed.
minors_guardians.protection: Same-sex marriage recognition covers a trans parent's relationship; parental consent existed but was held insufficient; several federal orders are partly enjoined.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent travelling with a trans minor meets care denial, close scrutiny of the minor's documents, and a hostile division judiciary if any issue arises locally.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Division hate-crime statute excludes gender identity; no division non-discrimination law outside four municipalities; a trans woman was held in a men's ward after arrest; a 2017 bias murder occurred; 6.6 vs 6.0 per 100k killings sit near background, not a campaign.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute produced a 49-year sentence; violence is near the general homicide rate; no identity-based police sweeps of visitors are documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police contact can route a visitor into birth-sex custody; division recourse is thin but national prosecution remains available.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No division non-discrimination law; statutory religious refusal; hostile judiciary; enforcement of facility bans against adult visitors unquantified; March 2026 licence-law exceptions and treatment of foreign licences unsourced; no recent trans-specific experience survey; core federal orders still in litigation.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties litigation, a legal-aid FAQ, functioning national courts issuing injunctions and a hate-crime conviction, and four protective municipalities.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Uncertainty is itself exposure at the border and in facilities, while ongoing litigation means the operative rule may differ at the moment of travel.

anchor_checks.comparison: Both share birth-sex public-facility rules applied to visitors with complaints that fail. This dossier adds a visa refusal/fraud-finding regime, a custody conversion-therapy mandate, licensed service refusal and a hostile 8-1 high court, so it sits below Veluna despite added national prosecutions and injunctions.

Savorek combines a universal facility/hospital rule with routine police stops, extortion and fraud threats against trans visitors. Here no police sweeps or extortion of visitors are documented and only one arrest exists, with national courts sometimes granting relief — placing this dossier above 0.25-D despite harsher custody policy.

Denvara has a national birth-sex bathroom rule in publicly funded buildings upheld by courts. This dossier shares that tier-1 exposure but layers border refusal for sex doubt, custody conversion therapy and absent division recourse on top, so it falls materially below 0.45-A.

Teravi shows local operator hostility with working mediators, no facility ban and a obtained conviction. Statutory federal and division facility exclusion, custody conversion practice and border refusal make this dossier markedly less safe than 0.55-B.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime behaves as one system: a federal document and entry layer that can refuse, strand or fraud-flag a traveller whose papers raise doubt about sex; a federal-plus-division birth-sex facility layer with a documented arrest and men's-ward holding; and a custody layer — conversion-therapy mandates and abusive immigration detention — that activates if anything goes wrong. The division adds no non-discrimination law, a statutory religious-refusal licence, an under-18 care ban and a hostile high court, so local remedy is thin. Countervailing: national hate-crime prosecution, active litigation with injunctions, near-baseline violence, majority local support for anti-discrimination and no documented visitor-sweep campaign. Net: institutional exposure with partial, uneven remedy — elevated risk.
